t: A Hohenzollern kingdom proclaimed at Königsberg in 1701, built from scattered lands between the Rhine and the Baltic.
Its army and disciplined bureaucracy made a poor, small state a European great power under Frederick II.
Under Bismarck it defeated Denmark, Austria and France and in 1871 united Germany under its king.
dyk: Prussia’s first king was only ‘King in Prussia’, because part of Prussia still belonged to Poland; Frederick II took the title ‘King of Prussia’ after the partition of 1772.
ev: Elector Frederick III crowns himself Frederick I, King in Prussia, at Königsberg
Frederick II invades the Habsburg province of Silesia
The Peace of Hubertusburg ends the Seven Years’ War; Prussia keeps Silesia
The First Partition of Poland gives Prussia West Prussia
Napoleon defeats Prussia at Jena and Auerstedt
The Congress of Vienna grants Prussia the Rhineland and Westphalia
William I is proclaimed German Emperor at Versailles

f.capital: Berlin (Königsberg the coronation city; Potsdam a royal residence)
f.founder: Frederick I (Elector Frederick III of Brandenburg)
f.predecessor: Brandenburg-Prussia (Margraviate of Brandenburg and Duchy of Prussia)
f.successor: Free State of Prussia (within the German Reich)
